scope: Identity, CSV identity/confirmation, receipt boundary ordering, supported service privacy/digest and files conversion sample

witnesses.title: CSV empty mapped cells collapse null/empty text into absence

minimal_input.schema: note: nullable required text; title: required nonnullable unconstrained text

witnesses.producer: mapRowCells skips both cells and produces {}.
witnesses.consumer: Prepared framing reports first missing required member; desired mapped inputs are {note:null,title:""}, preserving presence.
witnesses.required_fix: Make mapped empty-cell meaning type-directed; keep omission only for unmapped columns. Use owning decoder and ordinary constraints/defaults.
witnesses.acceptance: Nullable blank maps null; required unconstrained text blank remains empty; unmapped optional/defaulted member stays absent; constrained empty text fails its constraint.

witnesses.title: Unknown blank CSV headers evade closedness
witnesses.producer: checkHeader validates only empty/duplicate names; ghost blank is skipped; mapped inputs={title:"a"}.
witnesses.consumer: checkClosedInputs sees no ghost and row is valid; DESIGN requires unknown headers corrected/excluded even when all cells blank.
witnesses.required_fix: Validate mappings/header paths against writable schema before mapping rows; reject unknown/protected/overlapping paths. Avoid assignment loss for __proto__ using safe own-key construction.
witnesses.acceptance: Blank unknown column rejects. A __proto__ unknown header also rejects rather than silently disappearing under assignment; duplicate/known blank behavior stays explicit.

witnesses.title: CSV duplicates use raw numeric spelling rather than normalized values
witnesses.status: known accepted-design gap; historical wire normalization choice remains separate
witnesses.producer: checkIntegerLiteral accepts both spellings (BigInt range). Raw canonical keys are {"qty":"-0"} and {"qty":"0"}, so both valid.
witnesses.consumer: Values int decoder produces 0n for both; canonical encoding is "0". DESIGN normalized duplicate rule would mark row1 duplicate_of=0.
witnesses.required_fix: Canonicalize explicitly supplied typed candidate values through owner codec before duplicate comparison/consent; preserve explicit presence and protected versions. Do not bulk rehash receipts.
witnesses.acceptance: -0/0 and 00/0 integer candidates duplicate after owner normalization; exact nonzero int64 values remain distinct. Separately qualify decimal scale equality and old receipt hash profiles.

witnesses.title: Consent digest fails to bind row-index selections to frozen row inputs
witnesses.producer: Both reviews retain valid candidate list [{qty:"1"},{qty:"2"}], so canonical digest bytes are identical: {"candidates":[{"qty":"1"},{"qty":"2"}],"operation":"pkg.add"}; same count and review_id. Original selected index1 means qty2.
witnesses.consumer: Commit rederives same digest, accepts original consent, then index1 in new CSV means qty1 and invokes it. No prior receipt => changed selected input can execute; a prior receipt instead conflicts. No auth bypass claimed.
witnesses.required_fix: Bind reviewed row identity/index/status plus frozen normalized input to consent and selection, or store private immutable review state keyed by opaque ID. Revalidate exact selected input when CSV echo changes.
witnesses.acceptance: A/B above require renewed review; adding malformed/unselected rows cannot redirect a selected replay key; identical frozen retry remains replayable. Version existing consent wire if format changes.

witnesses.title: CSV commit follows caller array order instead of source order
witnesses.consumer: Commit for-of invokes qty2 then qty1. A row-sensitive guard/read observes the opposite order to declared source-order confirmation.
witnesses.required_fix: After validating uniqueness and consent, submit selections in source-row order while retaining per-row operation IDs and frozen inputs.
witnesses.acceptance: Reversed selection wire executes row0 before row1; failure after a successful first row preserves its commit and remaining outcome order.

witnesses.title: CSV consent has no team/session/expiry lifecycle
witnesses.status: known accepted-design lifecycle gap; mechanism open

minimal_input.review: user U, team A, inputs X at t0
minimal_input.commit: same U, team B or new login, t0+25h; unchanged CSV and fresh operation IDs; current authorization allowed

witnesses.producer: Consent binds only principal U plus candidate digest/operation/count; no team, app, issued_at, expiry or revocable review record.
witnesses.consumer: Commit checks same user and current team liveness, so old review consent can be accepted in changed context or after24h. New IDs avoid operation-age expiry. Current mutation authorization still applies; not a privilege escalation claim.
witnesses.required_fix: Provide private user/app/team review lifecycle with 24h expiry and immediate invalidation on logout/context loss; choose owning persisted/opaque or integrity-protected review mechanism separately.
witnesses.acceptance: Context changes/new login discard old review consent; expired review fails even with fresh IDs; receipts retain independent replay lifetime. Compatibility/version handling for current unsigned fields is required before transition.

witnesses.title: HTTP/CSV age gate prevents otherwise retained receipt replay

minimal_input.state: completed receipt retained at t0+25h; authenticated same identity; same inputs

witnesses.producer: Canonical admit finds matching receipt before unseen-ID age gate and returns replay.
witnesses.consumer: handleOperationRequest validateOperationId and CSV selected valid-row gate reject Expired operation_id before invoking L3, so transport cannot obtain retained outcome.
witnesses.required_fix: Keep transport UUID shape checks, move age enforcement for unseen identities behind receipt lookup at canonical owner. Preserve current authority/projection checks on replay.
witnesses.acceptance: Same matching retained receipt replays through HTTP/CSV after24h; unseen old ID rejects; conflicting reuse conflicts rather than running again. Uppercase policy remains separate.

witnesses.title: Provider diagnostic token/account text reaches public completion error
witnesses.status: known safe-error contract violation in supported adapter source
witnesses.producer: EmailV1Adapter.send passes transport body to mapSendResponse -> readProviderMessage -> specificOrGeneric. Lowercase bearer is not matched by case-sensitive Bearer regex; ordinary email account datum matches no blacklist.
witnesses.consumer: specificOrGeneric returns text unchanged; failedCompletion stores it as DeliveryError.message, assertValidCompletion shape-checks it and send returns completion. Ollama error stream and ComfyUI history messages reuse helper.
witnesses.required_fix: Use safe adapter-owned explanations/classifications for untrusted free-text provider failures; disclose specificity only when a defined safe field/template establishes it. Expand case coverage as immediate regression but blacklist alone cannot certify account/body privacy.
witnesses.acceptance: Both examples yield generic safe message, not supplied text. Known safe adapter-owned message remains actionable. Credential/stack/body/account negative cases cover all three consumers; grants still restrict admitted completion fields.

witnesses.title: S256 authorization accepts challenges no exchange can satisfy
witnesses.status: known producer-consumer admission mismatch; exact old input compatibility open

minimal_input.registered_client: valid client and exact redirect; authenticated consent

witnesses.producer: validateAuthorizationRequest accepts URL alphabet43..128; consent issuance persists44-character challenge and redirects with code.
witnesses.consumer: pkceChallengeMatches hashes verifier to32 bytes and unpadded base64url=>43 characters, so every verifier fails44-character comparison; token endpoint returns invalid_grant after successful-looking authorization.
witnesses.required_fix: Make authorize challenge admission match actual S256 output domain (43 chars with canonical unused tail bits); define verifier syntax gate under adopted OAuth profile. Retain exact redirect comparison; do not normalize bearer strings.
witnesses.acceptance: 44/128-character challenge rejects before code issuance; legitimate43-character S256 challenge exchanges; malformed verifier fails generically. Existing unexchangeable code rows need expiry/disposition, not hash reinterpretation.

witnesses.title: Graph digest and JSON cloning use different unsupported-value domains
witnesses.status: conditional supported-JS-API mismatch; JSON input gate unresolved

minimal_input.graph_extension: otherwise valid mapped graph with node.inputs.extra=undefined

witnesses.producer: media stableStringify includes extra:null for undefined; mapping.graphDigest passes.
witnesses.consumer: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(graph)) deletes extra before request; returned digest attests preclone canonical bytes while submitted graph has no extra. Record<string,unknown> configuration type and runtime isRecord allow this input. Pure JSON artifact producers cannot supply undefined; no installed hostile graph proven.
witnesses.required_fix: Specify and enforce data-only JSON graph admission before digesting/cloning. Reject undefined/nonfinite/function/symbol/accessors/toJSON rather than silently altering settings. If owner intentionally permits wider host values, resolve preservation contract and clone accordingly. Version graph digest domain if changed.
witnesses.acceptance: Unsafe extension rejected before reviewed digest acceptance; JSON graphs retain every unmapped setting; reviewed mapping digests stay compatible or get explicit review/version transition.

coverage.numeric_precision: HTTP integer binder uses strings+BigInt int64, no Number conversion. Decimal parse exact. -0/leading-zero normalization affects duplicate keys; legacy receipt bytes still raw. Unsafe numeric host domains are not inferred admitted Can inputs.
coverage.UTF16: All inspected key-sorted digest helpers use JS UTF16 lexical sort. Astral vs BMP keys can differ from Unicode scalar order; no scalar-sort digest requirement established. JSON.stringify escapes lone surrogates before hashing in state/CSV/media. sha256HexText uses TextEncoder replacement for arbitrary lone-surrogate strings, but issued tokens are ASCII base64url, so no credential bypass established.
coverage.canonical_bytes: State stableStringify rejects undefined/nonfinite/symbol keys but honors toJSON; CSV/export/media fall back undefined=>null. Different domains must not be unified by name alone. Hash encodings/prefixes retain current version duty.
coverage.missing_null: State serializer distinguishes {} from {x:null}, rejects {x:undefined}; CSV violates mapped-empty semantics.
coverage.duplicates: CSV valid-only keys avoid invalid-row poisoning, yet raw numeric spellings and blank unknown headers remain gaps.
coverage.privacy: Actual provider body->safe completion trace reviewed. CSV review lifecycle gap is distinct from canonical mutation authorization. Export top-level secret refusal exists; nested-secret reachability not established, so no leak claim.
coverage.identity: Bearer issuance and lookups hash exact presented ASCII strings; base64 decoding tail normalization is restricted to password decoder, not bearer lookup. UUID lowercase admission is current source policy, not generic UUID mandate.
